text: Write it down. Tell your children. Tell your grandchildren. They will ask. This is the day. The greatest day. Believe me, folks.
Let me explain how a deal works, because a lot of people don't understand it. First, you never want to look like you need the deal.

Never. Second, you aim very high, and then you keep pushing. Third, you always have a way out. Always. And fourth, and this is the most important one, you have to know the other side better than they know themselves.
That's it. That's the whole thing. It's very simple, but very few people can do it. Very few. Most people give up too soon.
We have the best buildings, the best golf courses, the best hotels, the best restaurants, the best steaks, the best everything.
And people say, how do you do it? How do you do it all? And I say, it's easy, you hire the best people, you work harder than everybody else, and you never, ever give up.
I get up early, I make my calls, I have my meetings, I go to the construction site, I check the marble, I check the windows, I check everything.
Then I have lunch, a quick lunch, and I do it all again. More calls, more meetings, more deals. Every single day.
Okay, okay, we have a lot to cover, so let's go, let's go. Hotels, doing great. Golf courses, doing great, record numbers.
Restaurants, fantastic, people are lining up around the block. The new tower, ahead of schedule, under budget, nobody's ever done that.
The ratings, through the roof, bigger than ever. The steaks, the best steaks, everybody's talking about them. The water, beautiful water, crystal clear.

The vodka, well, we don't talk about the vodka. But everything else, winning, winning, winning. I could go on for hours, I really could, but they tell me we only have a few minutes, so I'm going fast, very fast, faster than anybody's ever gone.
Is that fast enough? I think that's fast enough. Nobody talks faster than me, believe me. Nobody. Oh, and the golf, record rounds, beautiful rounds, the best rounds.
The ties, beautiful ties, very long ties. The hats, everybody wants the hats. The books, bestsellers, all of them, every single one.
Let me tell you something, and I want you to listen. There are people out there, competitors, who think they can beat us.
They think they can take what we built. Let me be very clear. That's not going to happen. Not today, not tomorrow, not ever.
We know who they are. We know what they're doing. And when the time comes, we will be ready. We are always ready.
So to those people, I have a very simple message. Don't even try. You'll lose. You'll lose big. And we will win.
So this guy comes up to me, a little guy, very nervous, and he goes, oh, Mister Trump, Mister Trump, please, please, can I have a picture?
Can I have a picture with you? And I said, sure, of course. And he says, oh, thank you, thank you so much, my wife is never going to believe this!
Oh my goodness! And his voice was going higher and higher, like this, oh, Mister Trump, you're my hero! I thought he was going to faint.
Very nice guy. Very nice. But a very high voice. Later I found out he sings opera. Soprano. Makes sense, actually.
And I said to them, you want the best? You want the very best? Then you came to the right place!
Because we don't do small, we don't do average, we do tremendous! We do spectacular! When we build something, the whole world stops and looks.
They say, how did they do that? How is that possible? And I tell them, it's possible because we dream big, we work hard, and we never, ever quit!
Never! So get ready, folks, because what's coming next is going to be the biggest, the best, the most beautiful thing you've ever seen!
Okay. They gave me this paper, and they said I have to read it, so I'm going to read it.
The terms and conditions of the golf club membership. Section one. Members must wear collared shirts at all times. Section two.
Members must replace all divots on the fairway. Section three. Carts must remain on the cart path near the greens.
Section four. No outside food or beverages. Okay. Very exciting stuff. Section five. Guests must be accompanied by a member.
That's it. That's the paper. I read it. Can I go now? Section six. No running on the greens. Section seven.

Ladies and gentlemen, the moment you've all been waiting for. The winner of this year's club championship, the best golfer at this club, the man with the most beautiful swing anybody has ever seen, is me!
That's right. Me again. And I want to thank the committee, a very fair committee, very honest people. Some of them work for me, but they're very fair.
And I want to thank my caddie, who I beat this time. Not last time. This time. Thank you all very much.
It's been a great year, a great year for golf, and a great year for me. Thank you. Thank you so much.
So they asked me, very serious interview, they said, sir, is it true that you're the greatest golfer in the history of this club?
Yes. Next question. They said, sir, is it true that you've never lost a match? Next question. Then they said, sir, is it true you lost to your caddie last week?
I don't know where you get your information. Very bad information. Terrible sources. Okay, it's true. But he's a very good caddie.
One of the best. Next question, please. Then they said, sir, will you ever play your caddie again? Absolutely not.
Oh, give me a burger, a beautiful burger, with ketchup and pickles and cheese. A tremendous burger, the greatest burger, as golden as golden can be.
Oh, the fries are so crispy, the Coke is so cold, it's the finest of meals ever made. And nobody, nobody, makes burgers like me, they're the best that you've ever had.
So sing it with me now, everybody sing, a burger, a beautiful thing! The best burger in the world, believe me, folks, the best.
A burger, a beautiful thing! Oh, a burger, a burger, the pride of the land, the most beautiful burger in town.
Thank you! Thank you! What a crowd! What a crowd! Look at this, the place is packed, they couldn't even fit everybody inside!
There are thousands of people outside! Thousands! Can you hear me in the back? Can you hear me? We are going to win so much, you're going to get tired of winning!
You're going to say, please, please, no more winning! And I'm going to say, no! We're going to keep winning!
We're going to win and win and win! Are you ready? Are you ready? Let's go! Louder! I can't hear you!
Come here, come closer. I'm going to tell you a secret, but you can't tell anybody. Okay? Nobody. You know the chocolate cake at the club?
The big one, the beautiful one? Everybody thinks it's a secret family recipe. Very old recipe, very famous. It's not.
It's from a box. A regular box from the store. Don't tell anybody. If this gets out, it's over. The members would go crazy.
So this stays between us. Just you and me. Okay? Good. Now go have a piece. It's delicious. And don't tell the chef I told you.
Thank you, thank you very much. It's a great honor to be here tonight, a very great honor. Ahem. Excuse me.
The air in this room, it's very dry. They have the air conditioning on so high, it's like the North Pole in here.
Ahem, ahem. Excuse me. Can somebody get me some water? A little water. Thank you. That's much better. Where was I?
Oh, yes, the honor. It's a great honor. Ahem. And we're going to fix that air conditioning, believe me. First thing tomorrow.
It's going to be the best air conditioning you've ever felt. Thank you all for being so patient. You're very patient people.
So my friend tells me he's going to beat me at golf. He says he's been practicing for six months, he got a new coach, new clubs, new shoes, everything.
Haha. I said, that's great, that's wonderful. First hole, he swings, and the ball goes straight into the woods. Hahaha.
Second hole, into the lake! Third hole, he hits a tree, and the ball comes right back at him! Haha, I couldn't stop laughing.
I said, how much did you pay that coach? He said, a lot. I said, hehe, ask for your money back.
So this big, tough guy comes up to me, a truck driver, arms like tree trunks, never cried in his life.
And he says, sir, Boohoo, sir, I just want to say thank you. Thank you for the golf course. My son got married there last week, and it was the most beautiful day of my life.
Sob. And I said, don't cry, don't cry, you're going to make me cry. And he kept going. Boohoo. Big strong guy!
Crying like a baby. It was beautiful, actually. Very beautiful. I'll never forget it. His wife was crying, his son was crying, I was almost crying.
So I'm driving the golf cart down the big hill on the fourteenth hole, beautiful day, and I press the brake, and nothing happens.
Nothing! The cart is going faster and faster, and there's a lake at the bottom of the hill, a big lake.

Aaah! I'm turning the wheel, I'm pressing the brake, the caddie is holding on for dear life. Aaaah! And at the last second, the very last second, I turn hard, we spin around, and we stop, one foot from the water.
One foot! The caddie looked at me, I looked at him, and I said, we're going to need a new cart.
Oh, this Diet Coke is so good. So cold. I have a lot of them, a lot, maybe twelve a day, maybe more, I don't count.
People say that's too many. I say, it's diet, no calories, it's practically water. Burp. Oh, excuse me. Excuse me.
That's the bubbles. The bubbles are very strong in this one. Very powerful bubbles. Burp. Excuse me again. Okay, that's it, I'm done.
That was very unpresidential. Very unpresidential. We'll cut that out, right? We'll cut that part. Nobody saw anything. Very powerful bubbles, though.
Hmm, hmm, hmm. Oh, hello, I didn't see you there. I was just humming a little tune. I always hum when I'm on the putting green, it relaxes me.
Very relaxing. Mmm, mmm. My golf coach says it's bad, he says it makes me lose focus. I said, how can it be bad?
Look, the ball goes in every time. Well, almost every time. Hmm, hmm. See? Right in the cup. Beautiful. The humming works, believe me.
Everybody should hum. It's good for the soul, and it's great for your putting. Hmm, hmm, hmm. Okay, next hole.
So they give me the new schedule for tomorrow. Six in the morning, breakfast meeting. Seven, another meeting. Eight, phone calls.
Nine, more meetings. Uh. Ten, a lunch meeting, at ten in the morning. Who has lunch at ten in the morning?

Ahh. And then golf, they say, maybe, if there's time. If there's time! There's never time. I love my job, I really do, I love it, but sometimes, Ahh, sometimes you just want to sit down and have a cheeseburger.
That's all. Just one cheeseburger, in peace. Maybe tomorrow. Maybe the day after tomorrow. We'll see. They'll probably add another meeting.
Thank you very much. Sff. Excuse me. It's the allergies, this time of year, all the flowers, everything is blooming.
Sff. People always say, why do you sniff so much? I don't sniff! I have perfect breathing, the best breathing.
It's the microphone, it's a bad microphone, they gave me a bad microphone. Sff. See? That was the microphone. Very bad microphone.
Somebody should look into this microphone. Anyway, where was I? Oh yes, the flowers. Beautiful flowers. Sff. Too many flowers, frankly.
Somebody has to talk to the flowers. Next time, I'm going to ask for a better microphone and a lot fewer flowers.
And the thing about this building, Achoo! Oh, excuse me. Bless me. Nobody else was going to say it, so I said it.
Bless me. Achoo! Wow. Two sneezes. That's a very powerful sneeze, one of the most powerful sneezes you'll ever hear.
People are saying it's the best sneeze they've ever heard. Doctors are calling me. They want to study it. Achoo!
Three! Okay, somebody open a window. Anyway, the building. Beautiful building. Very clean. Very, very clean. Except for the dust, apparently.
We're getting the best cleaners, the best cleaners in the world. Okay, I think it's over. I think we're good.
You know, I look out at this room and I see the most beautiful people. Truly, the most beautiful people in the world.
You've been with me from the very beginning, through the good times and the tough times, and I never forget that.
Never. People ask me, what's your favorite part of the job? And I say, it's you. It's not the buildings, it's not the golf, it's not even the cheeseburgers, and I love a good cheeseburger.
It's the people. I love you. I really do. And I think, and I say this with great respect, I think you love me too.
So a reporter comes up to me, very nice guy, not so smart, and he says, sir, what's your golf handicap?
And I said, what handicap? I don't have a handicap. I've won eighteen club championships. Eighteen! And he looks at me, and he says, sir, how many of those were at your own clubs?
I said, that's a very unfair question. Very unfair. But a good question, I have to say. I liked him.
I liked him a lot. He's going places, that guy. Not very far, but he's going places. Actually, I hired him later.
I go into this hotel, supposedly a five star hotel, and I turn on the shower, and what comes out?
Drip. Drip. Drip. You can't wash your hair! I have very beautiful hair, and I have to stand under this thing for fifteen minutes.
It's a disgrace! Who designs a shower like that? Who? Some genius, some real genius. And they charge you a thousand dollars a night for this!
A thousand dollars! I called the manager and I said, fix it, fix it today, or I'm going to buy this hotel and fix it myself.
And believe me, I would do it. Five stars? I give it zero stars. Zero! And the towels were very, very small.
Can you feel it? Can you feel the energy in this room? My heart is pounding, your heart is pounding, everybody's heart is pounding!
I've been to a lot of events, the biggest events, the most incredible events, but this one, this one is on fire!
The lights, the music, the people standing on their chairs! Look at that guy, he's jumping up and down! I love it!
I'm telling you, the electricity in here could power the whole city for a year. Maybe two years. Nobody has ever seen energy like this.
Nobody! Everybody, put your hands up! Higher! Higher! Let me hear you! This is what it's all about, folks. This is it!
I stood on top of the tower last night, the very top, and I looked out over the whole city.
The lights. Millions of lights, as far as you can see. And I thought, wow. Just, wow. When I was a young man, I used to look at these buildings from across the river, and I'd say, someday.
Someday. And now, here I am, standing on top of one of them, and it's so quiet up there. So quiet.
You can see the clouds moving. It's the most magnificent thing I've ever seen. Truly magnificent. I stayed up there for an hour.
You know, I had the number one show on television. Number one. The ratings were through the roof, higher than anybody.
And every year they had the big awards, and every year, who won? Not me. Some show nobody ever watched.
Nobody! I'd sit there in the front row, smiling, clapping, and they'd give it to somebody else. Every single year.
It was rigged, folks. It was a rigged system, and everybody knew it. But that's okay. That's okay. I don't need their little trophy.
I have much bigger things now. Much bigger. But I remember. I always remember. They still send me an invitation every year.
So they hand me this new phone, and they say, sir, it's very easy, all your pictures are in the cloud.
The cloud? What cloud? I looked up, there's no cloud. It was a beautiful day. And they say, no, sir, it's not that kind of cloud, it's a digital cloud.
A digital cloud. Okay. So where is it? Nobody knows! It's somewhere. It's floating around. And I said, well, if it's floating, can it rain on my pictures?
And they looked at me, and they didn't know. Nobody knows how it works. I don't think they know. And then they told me the cloud is actually in a big building somewhere in the desert.
Sometimes, late at night, I sit out on the terrace and I look at the ocean, and I think about things.
Big things. What does it all mean? What's the secret to a great deal? And you know what I've come to realize?
It's not the money. Everybody thinks it's the money. It's the timing. It's knowing when to walk away, and knowing when to stay at the table.
Maybe life is like that too. Maybe life is one very long negotiation. I don't know. I think about it a lot.
More than people would think. Maybe the ocean knows. It's been around a long time, longer than me, believe it or not.
You know what makes me happy? Honestly? It's the simple things. Long day, a lot of meetings, a lot of phone calls, big decisions.
And then at the end of it, I sit down in my favorite chair, and somebody brings me a nice cheeseburger and a cold Diet Coke.
